svg.text: Flywheel next — the map model: bounded contexts, elements by kind, relationships typed by the DDD patterns, homes, and scope computed, never chosen

a context is a card · its elements have kinds from a vocabulary, not layers or lanes · a relationship carries a pattern with U and D and end markers · every element names its home · a claim attaches to an id and its scope is the homes of what it attaches to
id ordering · ref ordering/boundary · settled · home orders-svc
language: order — a customer's request to buy, placed to fulfilled · line — one product and quantity on an order
ELEMENTS · by kind, no layers, no lanes
tags filter, colour and group the drawing; a lane or a tier is a tag, a store is a kind an organization adds (2.5)
the attachment lives in the claim's chapter block (97) · scope: the element's effective home → orders-svc (200)
AT REST the card shows counts and chips, not boxes
a decision marker · settled plain, candidate soft, open with ?
every id: name as the book writes it, the chapter that states it, status settled · candidate · open (open paired with a question) (198)
two complete maps, current and target, one schema and vocabulary; one difference keyed on id: added · removed · changed · moved (121, 201)
the map moves only through the tools: attach · detach · set-home · map-edit (no ref, no map) · set-status · capture · mark-reviewed · add-repository (211)
one relationship per pair · the patterns are fixed (1.1)
id billing · ref billing/boundary · settled · home ledger-svc
two home chips: this context's elements are built in two repositories · a verdict dot per home (5.1)
open · the question travels with the element
Is the invoice store its own repository, or a schema inside ledger-svc?
shown with the element · captured in one gesture, source the map, pointer the id (201, 112)
VOCABULARY · shipped, extended by the organization (208)
flywheel/map-vocabulary.yaml: store extends service · facet lane [control, data]
the relationship patterns, the status values, the ref rule and the four types are never extended (3.4)
a link across contexts must cross a relationship that is not separate-ways (2.4)
an external context homes nothing and is drawn dashed; big ball of mud is hatched (2.1)
a session moves the map only in a writeback that also writes the chapter (120, 211)
homes Order · OrderPlaced · Orders API · Orders service
derived from kind and home only, never from tags (199)
joined the fleet when the target map first homed something in it (202)
the manifest names git details only · an unknown home or an unhomed entry fails the check (199)
SCOPE · computed from the target map through homes (200)
one ledger cell · the element's effective home
both contexts' scope: each home, each with its own verdict (105)
a relationship or a link is in scope for both ends
the invariant (4.8): only a home moved, a re-attachment
or a claim version moves a verdict
a tag, a kind, a facet, a derivation row or a
vocabulary change moves none; scope never reads
derivation and derivation never reads tags
re-attaching is one response: attach or detach on a claim (193, 211)
the target map underneath, always · overlay 1: current → target, the design difference · overlay 2: target at the operator's last review → target now (122) · one difference engine, keyed on id

added drawn with a plus · removed ghosted · changed with a delta and the fields on hover · moved with the old home struck through · repositories and claims are chips, never nodes · layout computed, fit the only camera command (5.5)
a relationship · pattern named on the edge, U and D at the ends, OHS · PL · ACL badges
a link between elements, typed by the vocabulary
a claim attached to an id (200)
scope, computed · a ledger cell per home

a context map in domain-driven design's terms: contexts, the elements they name, relationships typed by the fixed patterns, links between elements; element kinds, link kinds and facets from a shipped vocabulary the organization extends (198)

nothing is declared by hand: kinds and capabilities are derived from what a repository homes, scope from the attachments; a repository joins the fleet when the target map first homes something in it (199, 200, 202)

the map moves only through the tools of 193, and a session moves it only in a writeback that also writes the chapter; every construction session's work order names the elements it builds, their homes and the claims attached there (211)
